memory_candidates.content: When converting a mechanical write-idiom across many files where a plan's pre-implementation site-count hypothesis is used to size phases, expect substantial per-file overcounts when prose-only descriptions of a write (numbered-list steps describing what to update, without a literal code fence) are mistaken for literal grep-matchable sites during research/planning. In this task, 3 of 8 conversion-phase files had actual site counts 40-60% below the plan's hypothesis (task.md: 5 vs 6, todo.md: 3 vs 6, skill-todo/SKILL.md: 5 vs 12) because the bulk of their archival logic was pure prose/pseudocode. Always re-grep per-file immediately before editing rather than trusting the plan's count, and record the delta explicitly rather than silently converting a different number of sites than claimed.

git-commit-scoped.sh's auto-injected ephemeral-exclusion set for a specs/{NNN}_{SLUG}/ task directory pathspec (triggered when the positive pathspec ends with a trailing slash matching specs/[0-9][0-9][0-9]_*/) can trigger git's 'The following paths are ignored by one of your .gitignore files' hard failure when the directory's .lock subdirectory is itself gitignored -- passing an explicit :(exclude) pathspec for an already-ignored path causes git to treat it as an explicit reference and refuse the whole add, even though a plain (non-excluded) recursive add of the same parent directory silently skips the ignored path with no complaint. Workaround: pass the task directory pathspec WITHOUT a trailing slash (e.g. 'specs/957_foo' not 'specs/957_foo/') to git-commit-scoped.sh, which avoids matching the auto-exclusion regex and lets git's normal ignore-skipping behavior apply instead.
